coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK CONFIRMED: 2F q17-q27 = 2H q1-q11, eleven questions worth 40 marks. Predicted from the matching per-question mark sequence, then confirmed by reading. Coded in the same sitting as IGCSE-NOV24-F-P2; shared rows carry identical tags by construction.

GAP-CANDIDATE counting_elements_in_sets — q21, 4 marks. A three-set Venn with ALGEBRAIC entries, a condition given as n((A union B) complement) = 26, and an answer wanted as n(A complement intersect C). This is the strongest sighting of the cardinality form in the corpus: the notation is not decoration, it states both the given condition and the required answer, and the algebraic entries are spec Higher 1.5 A. Tagged venn_diagrams and solving_linear_equations as an INTERIM measure — solving for x is honestly covered; the counting and the algebraic set definitions are not.

q16 circle theorems split across parts: (a) is the angle at the centre with its reason, (b) is the isosceles triangle made by two radii, which is angles_on_lines_and_circles rather than a named theorem, and (c) is the cyclic quadrilateral.
q25 tagged areas_of_compound_shapes first: the shaded regions are an equilateral triangle minus its inscribed circle, and the triangle's area has to be built from the radius by trigonometry.
No arithmetic series and no calculus on this paper — both of this series' sightings were on Paper 1.
